gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a single BLUETTI Apex 300 can put out 240 V only through its NEMA 14-50R and shares one 3,840 W budget across that socket and all of its 120 V outlets, or that with the standard cord it passes only 1,800 W from the grid (3,840 W needs the optional 50 A cord), so a 240 V well pump or dryer plus the fridge must fit inside 3,840 W together and the cord has to be added to the cart.
standout_why: I compared against ecoflow.com/us/delta-pro-ultra, which I opened. It gives 7.2 kW per unit, 6 kWh expandable to 90 kWh, Smart Home Panel 2 with 12 circuits, and a soft-starter note for air conditioners, but shows no price and says nothing about the per-socket power budget or grid pass-through limits. tesla.com/powerwall returned 403. The Powerwall 3 datasheet PDF loaded but its text could not be read. ChatGPT's own answer says only that 'inverter power rating determines which appliances can operate simultaneously' and that 'transfer equipment, permits, and a qualified installer' are needed. None of these pages covers a shared 120/240 V budget, a pass-through limit that depends on the cord, or a measured transfer time. The finding is useful but does not decide the set: it applies to the BLUETTI kit, and the same check (240 V output budget and grid pass-through rating) also applies to the EcoFlow and Sun Gold Power sets.
kit_items: Inverter + battery head unit: BLUETTI Apex 300 (3,840 W continuous, 2,764.8 Wh, 120/240 V from one unit via NEMA 14-50R per StorageReview). It is the only approved-store unit I found that gives 240 V from one box at under $4k as a bundle.

Expansion batteries: 2 × BLUETTI B300K (each 2,764.8 Wh) for 8,294.4 Wh total. This is near the low end of the 10–15 kWh 'essential circuits' tier in ChatGPT's own table. StorageReview measured 7.38 kWh delivered from this setup (89%).

Grid/house connection: BLUETTI 50 A charging/bypass cord. StorageReview says the standard cord allows 1,800 W of pass-through and the optional 50 A cord allows 3,840 W. I did not look up this cord's store listing or price.
Home integration: a BLUETTI AT1 Smart Distribution Panel, or an electrician-installed transfer switch or interlock fed from the 14-50R. I could not price the AT1 from BLUETTI's store.

Alternative component set (separate battery + hybrid inverter, the '48 V / 51.2 V' route ChatGPT described): the Sun Gold Power SGH-11N2E-s kit, which is an 11.4 kW 48 V split-phase hybrid inverter plus 4 × 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4, enclosed cabinet, 2/0 AWG cables and a 300 A DC breaker in one cart. It needs a licensed install. The batteries are listed as CAN/RS485/RS232 compatible.

findings.label: 240 V output from a single unit and shared AC budget
findings.value: 240 V only on the NEMA 14-50R (120/240 V, 50 A); 3,840 W continuous shared across all outlets; the four NEMA 5-20R are two 1,920 W pairs
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Review: 3,840W, 240V, Grid Input Limit, UPS (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien)
findings.note: Front-panel 120V/240V selector; the four front outlets stay at 120 V in 240 V mode.

findings.label: Grid pass-through by cord
findings.value: 1,800 W with the standard cord; 3,840 W with the optional 50 A cord
findings.note: StorageReview: grid draw can be capped from 1 A to 50 A in 1 A steps; the battery supplies the rest. In 120 V mode on a 240 V supply the limit applies to one line. BLUETTI quotes up to 12 kW bypass via the P050A port, which StorageReview did not test.

findings.label: Measured utility-to-battery transfer time
findings.value: 16 ms (120 V, 20 ms mode, at ~100 W and ~700 W)
findings.note: BLUETTI's 0 ms mode applies to two front outlets in 240 V mode on 120 V input, which StorageReview did not capture.
